claims.head: Power against power
claims.call: The Flames’ L1 (Farabee, Backlund and Coronato) spends at least 68% of its 5-on-5 time against the Wild’s first line.
claims.body: At home, the Flames keep sending Coronato’s line (Farabee, Backlund and Coronato) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Huska has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Wild’s first line is Kaprizov, Ek and Boldy.
claims.nums: At home: 68% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 39% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Ryan Huska likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Wild’s first line.
claims.cite: Matchups · Calgary home games this season · 4 games, 38 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

chips.tip: Calgary’s L1 (Farabee, Backlund and Coronato) at home: 68% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ first lines. Matchups, Calgary home games this season, 4 games, 38 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 39% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

claims.body: The Wild play some of the league’s fastest games, and so do the Flames. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.

notes.text: Marcus Foligno is on injured reserve and has missed the last 6 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Jared Spurgeon has not dressed for the last 4 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Jonas Brodin has taken his spot beside Quinn Hughes.
Brock Faber is on injured reserve (skull surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-pair defenseman. Jonas Brodin has taken his spot beside Quinn Hughes.
Tyler Pitlick was added to the roster on Oct 13 and has played beside Michael McCarron and Rieger Lorenz.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 8 games cover only 32% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 8th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 41%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Samuel Honzek is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Joel Hanley has not dressed for the last 6 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Jake Middleton has taken his spot beside Zayne Parekh.
Connor Zary has not dressed for the last 5 games.
Jonathan Huberdeau is on injured reserve (hip surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.
Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 29% of the team’s shorthanded time in 8 games, up from 2% last season.

CGY.head: The Wild should be favored
CGY.body: Even though Calgary has home-ice advantage, Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Flames can still win it if they keep the shots coming, but a lot has to go their way.

MIN.head: This one sets up well for the Wild
MIN.body: Even though Calgary has home-ice advantage, Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Flames’ best way in is piling up shots.

items.text: Blake Coleman faces Calgary for the first time since leaving.
Jake Middleton faces Minnesota for the first time since leaving.
Quinn Hughes is two points from 500.

The Wild are newly without Maxim Shabanov, have been without Marcus Foligno and Jared Spurgeon for several games, and have had to make do without Filip Gustavsson and Brock Faber all season. Jesper Wallstedt is expected to start.
